Blaby's population increased by around 9,000 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 100,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Blaby increased by 9.6%, from just over 93,900 in 2011 to around 102,900 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the East Midlands (7.7%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Blaby was home to around 5.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 5.1 in 2011. This area was close to the median population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Blaby than across the East Midlands

Median age stable in Blaby

The latest census data also show that the average (median) age remained 42 years in Blaby between the last two censuses.

This area had a slightly higher average (median) age than the East Midlands as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 25 to 34 years rose by around 2,900 (an increase of 28.4%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 1,400 (6.5% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 25 and 34 years increased by 1.9 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Blaby stood out from other areas for housing

The percentage of households in the social rented sector increased in Blaby, but fell across the East Midlands.

In Blaby, the percentage of households in the social rented sector rose from 7.6% in 2011 to 8.2% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 15.8% to 14.9%.

Private renting in Blaby increased from 10.0% to 12.8%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 80.9% to 77.9%.

The rate of social renting in Blaby increased by 0.6 percentage points

Health in Blaby

In 2021, 49.2% of Blaby residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 46.7% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 36.1% to 34.6%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Blaby residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 0.9%, while those describing their health as "bad" was 3.2% (similar to 2011).

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in good health in Blaby decreased by 1.5 percentage points

Unemployment in Blaby

In 2021, 2.0% of Blaby residents (aged 16 years and over) said they were unemployed. This figure decreased from 2.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 6 in 10 people (60.3%) said they were employed (excluding full-time students), compared with 61.5% in 2011. The percentage of retired Blaby residents increased from 23.6% to 24.7%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were unemployed was greater across the East Midlands (1.4 percentage points, from 3.8% to 2.4%) than in Blaby (0.6 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 1.1 percentage points, from 4.0% to 2.9%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Blaby decreased by 0.6 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 9.0% of Blaby residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure decreased from 9.2% in 2011.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week remained 9.8% across the East Midlands. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Blaby decreased by 0.3 percentage points

Unpaid care in Blaby

In 2021, 5.0% of Blaby residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 8.1% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 50 people (1.8%) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.4% in 2011. The proportion of Blaby residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.4% to 2.5%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care was greater in Blaby (3.1 percentage points) than across the East Midlands (2.8 percentage points, from 7.4% to 4.6%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Blaby decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Blaby

In 2021, 8.3% of Blaby residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 6.1% in 2011. The 2.2 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the East Midlands, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 6.5% to 8.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 86.2% of people in Blaby identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 91.0% in 2011), while 2.7% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.6% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 1.0% in 2011 to 1.5% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 8.3% of usual residents in Blaby identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in Blaby

In 2021, 42.6% of Blaby residents reported having "No religion", up from 29.1% in 2011. The rise of 13.5 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Blaby. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the East Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.5% to 40.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 43.4% of people in Blaby described themselves as Christian (down from 58.1%), while 5.3% did not state their religion (down from 6.7% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 42.6% of usual residents in Blaby reported having "No religion"

Blaby residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 91,300 Blaby residents said they were born in England. This represented 88.7% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 85,800 in 2011, which at the time represented 91.4% of Blaby's population.

India was the next most represented, with just under 2,100 Blaby residents reporting this country of birth (2.0%). This figure was up from around 1,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.4% of the population of Blaby.

The number of Blaby residents born in Poland rose from just over 450 in 2011 (0.5% of the local population) to just under 1,100 in 2021 (1.0%).

In 2021, 88.7% of Blaby residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in Blaby

In 2021, 4.7% of Blaby residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 2.8% in 2011.

In 2021, 1.1% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.5% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Blaby that identified as "British only" increased from 15.9% to 55.9%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the East Midlands (2.7 percentage points, from 5.8% to 8.5%) than in Blaby (1.9 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Blaby increased by 1.9 percentage points

Family in Blaby

Of Blaby households, 18.1% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 19.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in five households (21.6%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 22.1% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children increased from 7.3% to 7.7%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater in Blaby (1.7 percentage points) than across the East Midlands (1.3 percentage points, from 19.5% to 18.2%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Blaby decreased by 1.7 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Blaby residents aged 16 years and over, 32.6% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 28.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (49.9%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 53.4% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Blaby that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.7% to 8.9%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in Blaby (4.0 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the East Midlands (3.8 percentage points, from 32.3% to 36.1%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Blaby increased by 4.0 percentage points

Disability in Blaby

In 2021, 6.1% of Blaby residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.2% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 10 people (9.6%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.1% in 2011. The proportion of Blaby residents who were not disabled increased from 83.6% to 84.3%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater across the East Midlands (1.6 percentage points, from 9.3% to 7.7%) than in Blaby (1.1 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Blaby decreased by 1.1 percentage points
